dim.immune.def: Chasm two, metrics → signals. Automate where it changes the economics of work; the human keeps the decision and the accountability.
dim.immune.name: Immune
dim.mutation.def: The capacity to change the model itself, not just adapt inside the one you have.
dim.mutation.name: Mutation
dim.playground.def: Chasm one, control → trust. Innovation recurring and protected inside the existing rhythm — not run beside it.
dim.playground.name: Playground
dim.reflex.def: Delivery works beyond a few teams: dependencies, alignment, a shared cadence. Without it, nothing above has a floor.
dim.reflex.name: Reflex
dim.signal-sensing.def: Processes, roles and governance redesigned around AI — and leading signals read before the lagging metrics move.
dim.signal-sensing.name: Signal Sensing
level.maturity.aware.body: The ideas are known and the language is in use, but the practices are occasional and depend on individuals. Nothing here is load-bearing yet.
level.maturity.aware.name: Aware but slow
level.maturity.blind.body: This state is not practised. What it protects against is happening unseen, and the dashboard will be the last to know.
level.maturity.blind.name: Blind
level.maturity.proactive.body: The practices run on a rhythm, with named owners, and survive quarterly pressure. The risk is success hardening — keep the correction clause alive.
level.maturity.proactive.name: Proactive and embedded
level.maturity.reactive.body: The practices run when something forces them — a miss, a crisis, a review. They work, late. The gap is cadence: make them routine before the next shock, not after it.
level.maturity.reactive.name: Reactive
level.maturity.selfmutating.body: The state corrects itself: the practices change the practices. Re-score on a cadence and treat a fall as the first signal.
level.maturity.selfmutating.name: Self-mutating
p.maturity.i1: The three rings. The NASA reporting-system precedent: log the unfamiliar, not the unhappy.
p.maturity.i2: A live SignalNet, or a suggestion box nobody reads?
p.maturity.i3: Athena detects. Humans decide. Governance records. Which of the three is missing?
p.maturity.i4: Governance latency: do you know your signal-to-decision time in days?
p.maturity.i5: The blind-spot register. Is there a page the rulebook would rather not have?
p.maturity.m1: Retired or rebuilt — not renamed. The rebrand doesn’t count.
p.maturity.m2: The leading-indicator dashboard: which of the Six Vitality Signals do you actually watch?
p.maturity.m4: Narrative coherence: could a new hire describe what you are for, in the current market?
p.maturity.m5: Mutation is maintained, not reached. When did you last re-score?
p.maturity.p1: When the last quarter got tight, what happened to the experiment budget?
p.maturity.p2: Name the last experiment that was stopped on its own criteria rather than by a calendar.
p.maturity.p3: The Candor Contract: when did someone last say the thing nobody wanted to hear — and what happened to them?
p.maturity.p4: Protect attention: are boredom breaks and uninterrupted blocks on the calendar, or only in the values deck?
p.maturity.p5: Choose two cells. Could you name the fourteen you are not playing?
p.maturity.r1: Think of the last release that needed several teams. Did it land when planned?
p.maturity.r2: Could anyone list this quarter’s top five dependencies today, without a meeting?
p.maturity.r3: Same cadence, same planning event — or a calendar of local plans stitched together?
p.maturity.r4: The Aggregation filter: by the time the number is on a slide, is it already too late?
p.maturity.r5: The Hierarchy filter: does a signal have to be cleared by a manager before it travels?
p.maturity.s1: Exhibit 2.1: lagging metric → the signal that moves first → Goodhart check → named listener.
p.maturity.s2: The two signal tests. A single loud complaint is noise; a quiet pattern that costs the sender is a signal.
p.maturity.s3: Redesigned means the steps changed, not that a tool was added to the old steps.
p.maturity.s4: Observe, don’t ask: behavioural telemetry before survey questions.
p.maturity.s5: Who met last week, how close to the customer, and what did they escalate?
p.placement.i1: Pick one autonomous action from last week. Who owns it, by name?
p.placement.i2: Could you show the before-and-after cost per unit for your largest automation?
p.placement.i3: If a customer challenged an automated decision tomorrow, could you replay it?
p.placement.m1: Retired or rebuilt — not renamed. The rebrand doesn’t count.
p.placement.m2: For each metric on the dashboard, is there a signal that moves first, with a named listener?
p.placement.p1: When the last quarter got tight, what happened to the experiment budget?
p.placement.p2: Name the last experiment that was stopped on its own criteria rather than by a calendar.
p.placement.p3: Where did the last shipped idea actually come from?
p.placement.r1: Think of the last release that needed several teams. Did it land when planned?
p.placement.r2: Could anyone list this quarter’s top five dependencies today, without a meeting?
p.placement.r3: Same cadence, same planning event — or a calendar of local plans stitched together?
p.placement.s1: Redesigned means the steps changed, not that a tool was added to the old steps.
p.placement.s2: Has any job description been rewritten because of what AI now does?
p.placement.s3: Does every AI system that acts have its own identity, owner and permission scope?
q.maturity.i1: Anyone can log something unfamiliar — from a supplier, a system or a person — without blame or consequence.
q.maturity.i2: Logged signals are clustered, ranked by how unfamiliar they are, and each cluster has a named listener.
q.maturity.i3: Where AI acts autonomously, a named human owns the decision and can explain it after the fact.
q.maturity.i4: We measure the delay between a signal being raised and a decision being made.
q.maturity.i5: We keep a register of what the current model has made us stop seeing, and every new version names what the last one got wrong.
q.maturity.m1: We have retired or fundamentally rebuilt a core part of our operating model in the last twelve months.
q.maturity.m2: Leading indicators — behaviour, language, workflow drift — sit on the dashboard beside the lagging ones.
q.maturity.m3: Someone was visibly rewarded in the last year for raising a signal that invalidated a plan.
q.maturity.m4: The story we tell about ourselves matches what we actually do this quarter — not the year we rebranded.
q.maturity.m5: We re-score our readiness on a cadence and treat a falling score as a signal, not a rounding error.
q.maturity.p1: A protected share of capacity goes to experiments every cycle — and survives quarterly pressure.
q.maturity.p2: Experiments run in small loops with pre-agreed success criteria, and some are expected to fail.
q.maturity.p3: People tell each other the uncomfortable truth early, and it is met with enquiry rather than blame.
q.maturity.p4: Deep-work time is protected; attention is treated as a budget, not an assumption.
q.maturity.p5: Leadership has circled two cells of the Innovation Matrix and visibly said no to the rest.
q.maturity.r1: Work that spans more than three teams reaches customers on a predictable cadence, without heroics.
q.maturity.r2: Cross-team dependencies are visible and managed before they become escalations.
q.maturity.r3: One planning rhythm governs all the teams that need to move together.
q.maturity.r4: Information reaches decision-makers in time to act — not aggregated into a report after the fact.
q.maturity.r5: People raise what they noticed without waiting for permission to say it.
q.maturity.s1: For each lagging metric on the dashboard, we know the signal that moves first — and who is listening for it.
q.maturity.s2: Before a signal is acted on, we ask whether it repeats and whether it costs the source something to send.
q.maturity.s3: At least one core process has been redesigned around AI rather than having a copilot added to it.
q.maturity.s4: We learn from how customers and systems actually behave, not only from what people say in interviews.
q.maturity.s5: A sensemaking cell close to the work meets on a cadence and can escalate without going through the hierarchy.
q.placement.anomaly: “That’s just noise” is a common response to odd data, user pushback or internal dissent, and there is no route to escalate it.
q.placement.brand: Customers, analysts and journalists still describe us by a product or era we are trying to move past.
q.placement.consulting: Headcount grows while product revenue stays flat; we solve with people what competitors solve with platforms.
q.placement.ecosystem: Fewer third parties integrate with us than two years ago, and top AI or engineering talent is choosing startups or rivals.
q.placement.i1: Where AI acts autonomously, a named human owns the decision and can explain it after the fact.
q.placement.i2: Automation was chosen where it changed the unit economics of the work — not where it was merely possible.
q.placement.i3: Every autonomous action leaves enough evidence to reconstruct what happened.
q.placement.m1: We have retired or fundamentally rebuilt a core part of our operating model in the last twelve months.
q.placement.m2: We track leading signals — behaviour, language, workflow drift — not only lagging metrics.
q.placement.m3: Someone was visibly rewarded in the last year for raising a signal that invalidated a plan.
q.placement.p1: A protected share of capacity goes to experiments every cycle — and survives quarterly pressure.
q.placement.p2: Experiments have pre-agreed success criteria, and some are expected to fail.
q.placement.p3: An idea from outside the leadership team shipped to customers in the last quarter.
q.placement.platform: Our tools are built for internal use; there is no API, SDK or developer program that others build on.
q.placement.r1: Work that spans more than three teams reaches customers on a predictable cadence, without heroics.
q.placement.r2: Cross-team dependencies are visible and managed before they become escalations.
q.placement.r3: One planning rhythm governs all the teams that need to move together.
q.placement.rd: We research and prototype far more than we ship — labs and pilots rarely reach the customer.
q.placement.s1: At least one core process has been redesigned around AI rather than having a copilot added to it.
q.placement.s2: Roles have changed because of AI — what people are accountable for is different than eighteen months ago.
q.placement.s3: Governance treats AI systems as actors with identity and scoped permissions, not as tools.
q.placement.talent: Our strongest builders and product leaders have quietly moved to edge roles, competitors or their own startups.
read.maturity.head: {level}.
read.maturity.weak: Weakest state: {weak} ({weakLevel}). Strongest: {strong}. Maturity is only as real as its weakest state — that is where the next workshop goes.
read.placement.all.body: Every state is holding. The risk now is success hardening — practices freezing into routines that stop being questioned. Re-score quarterly, and treat a falling Mutation score as the first signal, not a rounding error. Relapse to Reflex is one rebrand away.
read.placement.all.head: All five holding.
read.placement.floor.body: Iterative delivery at scale is not yet holding, so nothing above it has a floor. That is not a criticism — it is the honest place to start, and the state with the fastest, most visible payoff. Start by making the dashboard tell the truth.
read.placement.floor.head: You’re in Reflex.
read.placement.gap.body: You are operating in {at} while {weak} ({weakSub}) is not holding.
read.placement.gap.head: You’re in {at}.
read.placement.gap.stuck: Part of the team is still in {chasm}.
read.placement.gap.tail: This is the most common and most expensive pattern we see: the organization has climbed higher than its governance can support. The next move is not another state up. It is closing the gap beneath you.
read.placement.next.body: {holding} holding. {weak} ({weakSub}) is the leap in front of you — and only if the market demands it. Climbing higher than the problem requires is an expensive way to be wrong.
read.placement.next.head: You’re in {at}.
read.placement.red.reflex: The red panel disagrees, though: delivery holds, but the Seven Stagnation Signals read Reflex. That is the scoreboard being wrong — start with S1 Signal Mapping.
